# HomeLink: The Key to Your Home


For more than 30 years, HomeLink has helped drivers seamlessly activate garage doors and gates from the comfort of their vehicle.


What began as a simple way to replace the garage door remote with buttons built directly into the vehicle has grown into one of the most widely adopted vehicle-to-home technologies in the world.


But the home looks very different than it did 30 years ago. Connected locks, cameras, lights, thermostats, garage door openers, security systems, and other smart devices have transformed what is possible around the home. And as those technologies have multiplied, so have the ways homeowners need to interact with them.


That creates an opportunity for HomeLink to do what it has always done: make the connection between vehicle and home simpler.


#### The


Problem: A More Connected, More Complicated Home


The promise of the smart home has always been simplicity. But for many homeowners, adding more connected devices can introduce more complexity.


Different products may require different apps, accounts, subscriptions, interfaces, and ecosystems. Something as simple as arriving home could mean opening the garage, unlocking a door, turning on lights, adjusting the thermostat, and disarming a security system, each through a different interaction.


Meanwhile, one of the most important parts of that daily routine often sits outside the smart home ecosystem: the vehicle.


For millions of people, the vehicle is where the transition between "away" and "home" actually happens. It's where a connected home experience can naturally begin.


#### The


Solution: Make the Vehicle Part of the Connected Home


[HomeLink](https://homelink.com/) is expanding the connection between vehicle and home. Rather than requiring drivers to reach for another device or navigate another app, HomeLink brings smart home control into an interface already integrated into the vehicle.


Garage doors and gates remain an important part of that experience, but they're no longer the limit of what's possible. Through an expanding ecosystem of RF, Bluetooth, and cloud-based connectivity, HomeLink can connect drivers with a broader range of smart home devices and services, from garage doors and gates to locks, lighting, security systems, and more.


The result is a vehicle that doesn't simply bring you home. It becomes part of how you interact with it.


### HomeLink Solutions


Connecting the vehicle to the home is only one side of the equation. The home itself is becoming more connected and increasingly complex. That's where[HomeLink Solutions](https://solutions.homelinksmarthome.com/home) comes in.


HomeLink Solutions is Gentex's smart technology offering for residential and commercial properties. Rather than representing a single product or technology, HomeLink Solutions brings together a curated portfolio of smart technologies from Gentex and other providers to create solutions designed to work together.


The idea is simple: multiple solutions, one vendor. For builders, property managers, and other customers, that means working with one team that can help identify, source, distribute, and install the right combination of technologies for a property rather than navigating multiple vendors independently.


Those solutions can span the connected property, from access and security to automation and other smart technologies, while giving Gentex the flexibility to incorporate both its own innovations and technologies from trusted partners.


This distinction is important.


1. HomeLink connects the vehicle to the home.


2. HomeLink Solutions brings together the technologies within the property.


Together, they create an opportunity to connect experiences across both environments.


#### Connecting


An Open Ecosystem


For decades, the three HomeLink buttons have represented something remarkably simple: press a button and your home responds. That simplicity is something drivers love. What's changing is what can happen behind the button.


HomeLink connectivity can now extend beyond traditional RF control through Bluetooth, cloud-based services, smartphone integration, and connected home platforms, creating new opportunities to connect the vehicle with the technologies people use throughout their homes.


And no single company defines today's connected home. Homeowners increasingly mix products and services from different manufacturers, making compatibility more important than ever. That's why HomeLink isn't about creating another closed smart home ecosystem. It's about connecting the ecosystems that already exist.


Compatibility has been part of HomeLink from the beginning. As homes become smarter, that same principle is expanding to new brands, devices, and connected ecosystems.


The goal is simple: work with as many brands and technologies as possible to make the connection between vehicle and home more useful, more seamless, and more accessible.
